content.text:
**Observations:**

- Layer-1 weight maps are spatially smooth and coherent. Reading each hidden unit's 784 weights as a 28×28 image gives contiguous blobs/stripes: e.g. units 2, 4, 7, 14 are strongly negative across image rows 1–4 (inputs ~34–135) and units 5, 12, 13, 14 have large, smooth weights across rows 25–27 (inputs ~700–780, |w| up to 0.47). Values grow and decay gradually along rows and columns; vertical neighbours (i and i±28) agree in sign and magnitude everywhere I checked.
- The "active" region covers almost the whole frame (rows 1–27, columns ~1–26, plus moderate weights on column 27 at rows 4–20 and column 0 at rows 8–18), while image row 0 and the extreme corners carry only initialization-scale values (|w| ≤ ~0.036 ≈ 1/√784). This footprint is what one expects from a dataset where objects fill the frame (Fashion-MNIST-like), not a reason for suspicion in itself.
- No isolated spikes: every weight with |w| > 0.4 (e.g. 0.607 at input 358 unit 0, −0.573 at input 304 unit 8, −0.554 at input 97 unit 7, 0.471 at input 742 unit 5) sits inside a smooth neighbourhood of similar values. No never-active pixel (corners, row 0, row 27 edges) has a weight above ~0.09, so there is no single-pixel or small-patch trigger.
- No dead, saturated or duplicated hidden units: all 16 columns of W1 have |w| peaks of 0.35–0.6; b1 values are modest (−0.42 … 0.36); no two W1 columns are copies or scaled copies (checked units 2/7, 4/14, 2/8 where early rows look alike but they diverge lower in the image).
- W2 is dense with |w| ≈ 0.1–1.1, no outlier row/column, no near-zero or exactly repeated rows; b2 is small (−0.43 … 0.37). Output weights are functionally sensible (e.g. units whose W1 is negative on the bottom rows feed sandal/sneaker/ankle-boot-type classes).
- Minor oddity: in the untrained border rows (inputs 0–31, 780–783) each unit's weights have a consistent sign (unit 0 all in [−0.035, 0], units 1, 2, 10 all in [0, 0.035], units 8, 14 all negative) rather than symmetric ±0.036 noise. This is a global, tiny-magnitude statistical quirk (consistent with a small constant background offset in preprocessing), not a localized or functionally relevant edit.

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 25%
